newsitem.title: USA: Princess accepts Florida fare agreement.
newsitem.headline: Princess accepts Florida fare agreement.

text.p: Industry holdout Princess Cruises, a unit of British shipping group Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Co will pay $85,000 in investigative costs and adopt a new full-fare pricing policy, Florida's attorney general said on Tuesday.

Princess is the last major cruise line to accept the new pricing policy in deals hammered out after Florida Attorney General Bob Butterworth complained cruise lines operating from Florida were misleading passengers on advertised fares.
Butterworth, who filed a civil complaint in a Florida court in March against Princess, charged the cruise lines were adding "port fees" as high as $150 per passenger to published fares.

Such fees covered cruise-line operating costs, as well as government-agency fees for harbor use and other services but largely constituted a source of hidden revenues for the companies, Butterworth said. "Under the agreement, Princess Cruises will only advertise initial cruise ticket prices which accurately reflect the revenue to be kept by the company," Butterworth said in a news release.
Industry leader Carnival Cruise Lines, a unit of Carnival Corp, and seven other cruise lines have struck similar deals on pricing with Butterworth.

No company admitted wrongdoing in the agreements, and some industry executives have said the change to incorporating port fees into published fares had been initially resisted by some out of fears rivals would be advertising seeming-bargains.

A spokesman for Butterworth said the agreement with Princess also settles the civil complaint filed against the line. That complaint had sought $15,000 for each alleged violation by Princess of Florida consumer-protection laws.
Butterworth said Princess would pay $85,000 to cover investigative costs.
